processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s before homogenization.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature (1050 °C for this sample) at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set T so that the temperature difference between inside and outside of the sample was removed.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression at 1050 °C and 0.01 s^-1 to a maximum of 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was water-spray cooled (quenched).

structures.overall_structure: Hot deformation (60% compression) of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel produces dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grains; the compressed specimen shows three deformation zones (1 difficult deformation zone, 2 small deformation zone, 3 large deformation zone), with DRX degree increasing as zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1. The degree of DRX increases with increasing T and with decreasing ε̇ (Fig. 9).

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: DRX average grain size increases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (Fig. 10); at 1150 °C/0.01 s^-1 the grain size exceeds 70 µm, whereas at low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) DRX grains are small but insufficient with large remnant original grains.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical sample of Φ8 mm × 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression to a maximum of 60% (maximum true strain 0.92) using a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on both end faces.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: True stress–true strain (rheological) curve at T=1050 °C, ε̇=0.01 s^-1 (Fig. 3a): the curve rises to an early peak (peak strain ≈0.1–0.2) then softens to a plateau; the 1050 °C curve lies between the 1000 °C and 1100 °C curves at ε̇=0.01 s^-1.

characterization_methods.purpose: Carry out isothermal constant strain rate compression experiments and record the rheological stress curves used to build the constitutive/DRX models
characterization_methods.key_findings: Flow stress decreases with increasing T and with decreasing ε̇; provides the flow curve for the 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 sample.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, then prepared, ground, polished and etched
characterization_methods.purpose: Collect microstructure images and measure the DRX average grain size
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure varies across three deformation zones with DRX degree zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1; DRX grain size increases with T and decreasing ε̇.

characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain boundaries for optical/confocal microscopy

computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation fitting to determine the material constant C

analytical_models.model_name: Cingara-McQueen equation (Eq. 4: σ/σp = [ε/εp · exp(1 − ε/εp)]^C; Eq. 5: ln(σ/σp) = C[ln(ε/εp)+1−ε/εp])
analytical_models.equation_role: Give the material constant C by linear fitting ln(σ/σp) versus [ln(ε/εp)+1−ε/εp], and hence (Eq. 9) the critical strain ratio εc/εp
analytical_models.model_note: The C fit is given explicitly at 1050 °C and 0.01 s^-1 (Fig. 5); the derived εc/εp ≈ 0.452 is the general result from Eq. 9.

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation (Eq. 3: Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT))

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain rate characterizing the combined influence of T and ε̇ on rheological stress
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ = 56.29 corresponds to the 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 condition (Table 1).

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Average value within the experimental range of this paper (b0034).

analytical_models.model_name: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function (Eq. 1) and activation energy relation (Eq. 2: Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2)
analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the dynamic recrystallization activation energy Qp
analytical_models.model_note: Lumped/average activation energy for the alloy over the whole experimental range (900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1), not a single-condition value.

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression fitting of the flow-stress characteristic values against lnZ (Eq. 10) and construction of the DRX state diagram

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate critical, peak and steady-state strains/stresses to the Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: εc = 0.0093 lnZ − 0.43; σc = 1.0048(lnZ)^2 − 97.23 lnZ + 2379.08; εp = 0.020 lnZ − 0.94; σp = 0.98(lnZ)^2 − 94.21 lnZ + 2291.34; εs = 0.034 lnZ − 1.53; σs = 0.55(lnZ)^2 − 46.96 lnZ + 984.67. Fits: σc R = 0.947, εc R = 0.911, σp R = 0.957, εp R = 0.911, σs R = 0.956, εs R = 0.922 (Fig. 6). The DRX state diagram (Fig. 7) divides conditions into A work hardening, B partial DRX and C complete DRX.

computational_details.simulation_method: Mathematical regression with the Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm for the DEFORM-3D DRX grain-size model (Eqs. 11–12)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid plastic body, die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; friction of the billet–die contact interface set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient of billet and air set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation analysis and error test of predicted vs experimental grain size gave R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples; absolute error mostly within 3 µm (Fig. 11).

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict the DRX average grain size as a function of ε̇ and T (with fixed initial grain size and strain)
analytical_models.model_note: drex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338; general model for the low-density high-strength steel.

unmapped_findings: The paper reports a dynamic recrystallization (DRX) state diagram (Fig. 7) dividing hot-deformation conditions into A work-hardening, B partial-DRX and C complete-DRX zones in the lnZ–strain plane; the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs both increase with increasing lnZ (b0058, figure_007).

For this Fe-Mn-Al-C steel a fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086); the specific 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 condition of this sample is not listed among these optimum windows.

No optical micrograph is reported specifically at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1; the Fig. 9 micrographs at 1050 °C were obtained at ε̇ = 1 s^-1 (panel e), and the Fig. 9 panels at ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 were obtained at 1100 °C (panels a), so the microstructure image belonging to this exact sample is not available (b0060, b0063, figure_009).

The steel is reported as a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological (flow) stress decreases with increasing T and with decreasing ε̇; the peak stress at ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 decreased from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (a reduction of 82%) (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

Reproducibility of the compression experiments was checked using the same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch with the same composition under identical experimental conditions (b0018, b0021, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).

In the DRX average grain size vs temperature plot (Fig. 10) the grain size at every temperature ranks 0.01 s^-1 > 0.1 s^-1 > 1 s^-1 > 10 s^-1; at 1150 °C the 0.01 s^-1 curve reaches just below 80 µm while the 10 s^-1 curve stays near 20–25 µm, but no numeric value is printed for the 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 point (figure_010, figure_011).
The paper discusses general conclusions and a 'prospect' section proposing future multivariate (experimental-design/chemometric) studies, with no sample-specific data (b0088, b0089, b0090).
